item.title: Novo shares tumble by double digits on grim sales outlook
item.description: In contrast to Lilly’s optimistic forecasts, Novo cited pricing constraints and competitive pressure in predicting up to a 13% decline in 2026 profits.

item.title: Trump signs funding bill with PBM reforms, hospital-at-home and telehealth extensions
item.description: The funding package ends a partial government shutdown and enacts several healthcare policies, including preserving telehealth flexibilities in Medicare through 2027.

item.title: Eikon Therapeutics nets a $381M IPO amid burst of biotech offerings
item.description: The offering is one of four biotech IPOs that could price by Friday, and comes during the busiest week for such activity since early last year.

item.title: Express Scripts reaches ‘landmark’ settlement with FTC in insulin suit
item.description: The agreement announced Wednesday includes sweeping changes to the Cigna PBM’s business practices, including no longer preferring expensive drugs over cheaper equivalents on standard formularies and reshoring its controversial rebate aggregator.

item.title: Generate, an AI-driven Flagship startup, pitches an IPO
item.description: The biotech, which raised more than $800 million privately on the promise of artificial intelligence-aided drug discovery, is developing a potential competitor to the asthma treatment Tezspire.

item.title: Bayer details anticipated stroke prevention data for new blood-thinner
item.description: Asundexian cut the risk of an additional stroke by 26% in a large Phase 3 trial without accompanying safety issues, boosting the commercial outlook for an emerging class of anti-clotting drugs.

item.title: Novo, Lilly sputter as Hims launches knockoff GLP-1 pill
item.description: Novo is threatening litigation in response, while FDA head Martin Makary, without naming specific companies, said the agency would take “swift action” against those “mass-marketing illegal copycat drugs.”

item.title: Earnings roundup: AbbVie angst, a bifurcated vaccine market and Bristol Myers’ waiting game
item.description: Vaccine makers are seeing sales declines in the U.S. and upswings in Europe. Elsewhere, investors fretted over an AbbVie franchise and Bristol Myers pointed to a trio of narrative-changing trials.

item.title: Agomab, SpyGlass bank a combined $350M in biotech IPOs
item.description: The two offerings capped off the busiest week for new biotech stock issuances in a year.

item.title: White House’s online service for drug sales debuts with limited impact on prices
item.description: Select products from Pfizer, Eli Lilly and others will be sold at a discount, although the lower costs won’t be felt by many Americans whose medications are covered by insurance.
